paragraphs.29: These materials represent standard insulation in HV equipment and exhibit different dielectric behaviours, which is helpful for testing model. PD experiments were conducted using two electrode configurations for each material: a point-plane (pointed electrode to a flat ground) and a plane-plane (both electrodes flat) arrangement. This yielded four test setups in total: Nomex-Pointed (NP), Nomex-Flat (NF), Teflon-Pointed (TP), and Teflon-Flat (TF). Each configuration was stressed to induce partial discharges, and 100 PD signal instances were captured per setup. Thus, initially, we obtained 100 PD Signals for the four configurations (each corresponding to a PD event or sequence under that condition). Initially, for each of the four configurations: Nomex-Pointed (NP), Nomex-Flat (NF), Teflon-Pointed (TP), and Teflon-Flat (TF), 100 signals get acquired. The limited dataset size can create an overfitting issue in the PD Classification task. Therefore, it is managed by generating scalograms using wavelet decomposition with multiple mother wavelets (db1 to db4), resulting in four scalogram images per original signal. A total of 1600 samples (Nomex-Pointed: 400, Nomex-Flat: 400, Teflon-Pointed: 400, Teflon-Flat: 400) have been utilized to analyses the accuracy level of the proposed algorithm. Where NP and NF data used for class “Nomex” and, TP and TF data used for class “Teflon” on classification approach. The data was aggregated by insulation material to enable the model to learn material-type pattern recognition, independent of electrode geometry.

paragraphs.66: A multi-level wavelet decomposition is applied on each captured PD signal to prepare the data for machine learning and Deep learning classification task. Through energy profiling, we found that for the Nomex insulation, PD signals had the highest magnitude of energy in the detailed coefficients of DC1 for the NP configuration and DC4 for the NF configuration. Regarding Teflon-based signals, signals from the TP configuration were highest in DC5 detail and DC4 for the TF configuration. These differences reflect the high-frequency behaviour of discharge events specific to material and geometry. From this analysis, we selected two prominent levels per configuration and extracted coefficients using each of the four mother wavelets (db1 to db4) because We want to enhance data diversity and improve model generalization, scalograms were generated using Daubechies db1 to db4 which were effectively increasing variability in the dataset for training which are shown in Figure 3. Therefore, in total, we produced eight scalograms for each original PD signal (2 levels x 4 wavelets). Given that there were 100 original signals for each configuration in four different configurations (NP, NF, TP, TF), this indicates 1600 scalograms (800 for class Nomex, 800 for class Teflon) analysed for the binary classification task.
